It is situated 150 km south east of [[Kochi]] and 200 km north east of state capital city of [[Trivandrum]].{{cite web|url=http://www.cwc.nic.in/main/downloads/National%20Register%20of%20Large%20Dams%202009.pdf|title=National Register for Large Dams|year=2009|publisher=Central Water Commission|pages=194–197|access-date=30 November 2011|location=India|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721165130/http://www.cwc.nic.in/main/downloads/National%20Register%20of%20Large%20Dams%202009.pdf|archive-date=21 July 2011|url-status=dead}} It is located {{Convert|881|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} above the sea level, on the [[Cardamom Hills]] of the [[Western Ghats]] in [[Thekkady]], [[Idukki District]] of Kerala, India. It was constructed between 1887 and 1895 by workers under the command of [[Colonel (United Kingdom)|Colonel]] [[John Pennycuick (British engineer)|John Pennycuick]], and also reached in an agreement to divert water eastwards to the Madras Presidency area (present-day [[Tamil Nadu]]). It has a height of {{Convert|53.6|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} from the foundation, and a length of {{Convert|365.7|m|ft|0|abbr=on}}. The [[Periyar National Park]] in Thekkady is located around the dam's reservoir. The dam is built at the confluence of Mullayar and Periyar rivers. dam around 1899]] The Periyar river which flows westward of Kerala in to the [[Arabian Sea]] was diverted eastwards to flow towards the [[Bay of Bengal]] to provide water to the arid [[rain shadow]] region of [[Madurai]] in [[Madras Presidency]] which was in dire need of a greater supply of water than the small [[Vaigai River]] could provide. The dam created the Periyar Thekkady reservoir, from which water was diverted eastwards via a tunnel to augment the small flow of the Vaigai River. The Vaigai was dammed by the [[Vaigai Dam]] to provide a source for irrigating large tracts around [[Theni]], [[Dindigul]], [[Madurai]], [[Sivagangai]], [[Ramanathapuram]] districts. Initially the dam waters were used only for the irrigation of {{Convert|68558|ha|acre|0|abbr=on}}.{{cite web| author=Ministry of Water Resources| publisher=Govt. of India| title=Mulla Periyar Dam issue| url=http://mowr.gov.in/index3.asp?subsublinkid=751&langid=1&sslid=733| access-date=6 December 2011| date=2 December 2011| url-status=dead| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110828193337/http://www.mowr.gov.in/index3.asp?subsublinkid=751&langid=1&sslid=733| archive-date=28 August 2011| df=dmy-all}} Currently, the water from the Periyar (Thekkady) Lake created by the dam, is diverted through the water shed cutting and a tunnel to Forebay Dam near Kumily (Iraichalpalam). From the Forebay dam, [[hydroelectricity|hydel]] pipelines carry the water to the Periyar Power Station in Lower Periyaru. ==Design== [[File:Mullaiperiyar Dam section.png|thumb|Cross section of Mullaiperiyar dam After the completion of concrete backing by Tamil Nadu PWD]] The Mullaperiyar Dam is a [[gravity dam]] made with concrete prepared from [[limestone]] and "surkhi" (burnt brick powder), and faced with rubble.{{cite journal |last1=Pennycuik |first1=John |title=Pennycuik on the Diversion of the Periyar |journal=Minutes of the Proceedings |volume=128 |issue=Part 2 |pages=140–163|date=26 January 1897 |url=https://archive.org/stream/minutesproceedi13unkngoog#page/n153/mode/2up |access-date=9 January weight and the force of gravity to support the reservoir and remain stable. The main dam has a maximum height of {{Convert|53.6|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} and length of {{Convert|365.7|m|ft|0|abbr=on}}. Its crest is {{Convert|3.6|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} wide while the base has a width of {{Convert|42.2|m|ft|0|abbr=on}}. It consists of a main dam, [[spillway]] on its left and an auxiliary dam (or "baby dam") to the right. Its reservoir can withhold {{Convert|443230000|m3|acre feet|0|abbr=on}} of water, of which {{Convert|299130000|m3|acre feet|0|abbr=on}} is active (live) storage.{{cite book |last=Frye |first=Albert Irvin|title=Civil engineers' pocket book: a reference-book for engineers, contractors, and students, containing rules, data, methods, formulas and tables |url=https://archive.org/stream/civilengineerspo00frye#page/858/mode/2up |access-date=30 November 2011 |edition=2nd (corrected) |year=1918 |publisher=D. Van Nostrand Company |page=859}}{{cite web|title=Mullaperiyar Environmental Protection Forum v. Union of India (UOI) and Ors|url=http://www.ielrc.org/content/e0609.pdf|pages=1–2|publisher=Supreme Courth of India|access-date=30 November 2011|archive-date=16 December 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111216014733/http://www.ielrc.org/content/e0609.pdf|url-status=live}} ==History== ===Feasibility studies=== The unique idea of harnessing the westward flowing water of the Periyar river and diverting it to the eastward flowing Vaigai river was first explored in 1789 by [[Pradani Muthirulappa Pillai]], a minister of the Ramnad king Muthuramalinga Sethupathy, who gave it up as he found it to be expensive. The location of the dam had first been scouted by Captain J. L. Caldwell, Madras Engineers (abbreviated as M.E.) in 1808 to reconnoitre the feasibility of providing water from the Periyar river to Madurai by a tunnel through the mountains. Caldwell discovered that the excavation needed would be in excess of 100 feet in depth and the project was abandoned with the comment in his report as "decidedly chimerical and unworthy of any further regard". The first attempt at damming the Periyaar with an earthen dam in 1850 was given up due to demands for higher wages by the labour citing unhealthy living conditions.{{cite news|last=T|first=Ramakrishnan|title=A dam steeped in history and controversy|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Chennai/article2580008.ece|access-date=27 November 2011|newspaper=The Hindu|date=29 October 2011|location=Chennai, India|archive-date=1 December 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111201011412/http://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/chennai/article2580008.ece|url-status=live}} The proposal was resubmitted a number of times and in 1862, Captain J. G. Ryves, M.E., carried out a study and submitted proposals in 1867 for another earthwork dam, 62 feet high. The matter was debated by the Madras Government and the matter further delayed by the terrible famine of 1876–77. Finally, in 1882, the construction of the dam was approved and Major [[John Pennycuick (British engineer)|John Pennycuick]], M.E., placed in charge to prepare a revised project and estimate which was approved in 1884 by his superiors. ===Lease=== On 29 October 1886, a lease indenture for 999 years was made between the [[Moolam Thirunal|Maharaja of Travancore]] Moolam Thirunal Rama Varma, and the British Secretary of State for India for Periyar Irrigation Works. The lease agreement was signed by Dewan of Travancore V Ram Iyengar and State Secretary of [[Madras State]] J C Hannington. This lease was made after 24 years negotiation between the Maharaja and the British. The lease indenture granted full right, power and liberty to the Secretary of State for India to construct make and carry out on the leased land and to use exclusively when constructed, made and carried out, all such irrigation works and other works ancillary thereto. The agreement gave 8000 acres of land for the reservoir and another 100 acres to construct the dam. The tax for each acre was {{Indian Rupee}} 5 per year. The lease provided the British the rights over "all the waters" of the Mullaperiyar and its [[Drainage basin|catchment basin]], for an annual rent of {{Indian Rupee}} 40,000. In 1947, after [[Indian Independence Act 1947|Indian Independence]], Travancore and Cochin joined the Union of India and on 1 July 1949 were merged to form Travancore-Cochin. On 1 January 1950, Travancore-Cochin was recognised as a state. The Madras Presidency was organised to form Madras State in 1947. On 1 November 1956, the state of Kerala was formed by the [[States Reorganisation Act]]. The Kerala state government announced that the earlier agreement which had been signed between British Raj and Travancore agreement was invalid and needed to be renewed.{{Cite web |last=Service |first=Express News |date=2024-08-05 |title=Supreme Court to reexamine validity of Mullaperiyar lease deed |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/kerala/2024/Aug/05/supreme-court-to-reexamine-validity-of-mullaperiyar-lease-deed |access-date=2024-08-07 |website=The New Indian Express |language=en}} After several failed attempts to renew the agreement in 1958, 1960, and 1969, the agreement was renewed in 1970 when [[C. Achutha Menon|C Achutha Menon]] was Kerala Chief Minister. According to the renewed agreement, the tax per acre was increased to {{Indian Rupee}} 30, and for the electricity generated in Lower Camp using Mullaperiyar water, the charge was {{Indian Rupee}} 12 per [[kilowatt-hour]]. Tamil Nadu uses the water and the land, and the Tamil Nadu government has been paying to the Kerala government for the past 50 years {{Indian Rupee}} 2.5 [[lakh]]s as tax per year for the whole land and {{Indian Rupee}} 7.5 lakhs per year as surcharge for the total amount of electricity generated.{{citation |url=http://www.hindu.com/fline/fl2305/stories/20060324004210600.htm |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130125191317/http://www.hindu.com/fline/fl2305/stories/20060324004210600.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=25 January 2013 |location=Chennai, India |title=Verdict on Mullaperiyar |author=R. ===Construction=== [[File:Periyar National Park.JPG|thumb|Periyar National Park|214x214px]] In May 1887, construction of the dam began. As per "The Military Engineer in India" Vol II by Sandes (1935), the dam was constructed from limestone and "surkhi" (burnt brick powder and a mixture of sugar and calcium oxide ) at a cost of {{Indian Rupee}} 104 lakhs, was 173 feet high and 1241 feet in length along the top and enclosed more than 15 thousand million cubic feet of water. Another source states that the dam was constructed of concrete and gives a figure of 152 feet height of the full water level of the reservoir, with impounding capacity of 10.56 thousand million cubic feet along with a total estimated cost of {{Indian Rupee}} 84.71 lakh. The construction involved the use of troops from the 1st and 4th battalions of the [[Madras Pioneers]] as well as [[Portugal|Portuguese]] carpenters from [[Cochin]] who were employed in the construction of the coffer-dams and other structures. The greatest challenge was the diversion of the river so that lower portions of the great dam could be built. The temporary embankments and coffer-dams used to restrain the river waters were regularly swept away by floods and rains. Due to the coffer dam failures, the British stopped funding the project. Officer [[John Pennycuick (British engineer)|Pennycuick]] raised funds by selling his wife's jewelry to continue the work. In [[Madurai]], Pennycuick's statue has been installed at the state PWD office and his photographs are found adorning walls in peoples homes and shops. In 2002, his great-grandson was honoured in Madurai, a function that was attended by thousands of people.{{cite news|title=Mullaperiyar dam: An engineering marvel|url=http://ibnlive.in.com/news/mullaperiyar-dam-an-engineering-marvel/205900-60-118.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111129012257/http://ibnlive.in.com/news/mullaperiyar-dam-an-engineering-marvel/205900-60-118.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=29 November 2011|access-date=6 December 2011|newspaper=[[CNN IBN]]|date=26 November 2011}} The dam created a reservoir in a remote gorge of the Periyar river situated 3,000 feet above the sea in dense and malarial jungle, and from the northerly arm of this manmade waterbody, the water flowed first through a deep cutting for about a mile and then through a tunnel, 5704 feet in length and later through another cutting on the other side of the [[water divide|watershed]] and into a natural ravine and so onto the Vaigai River which has been partly built up for a length of 86 miles, finally discharging 2000 [[Cubic foot#Cubic foot per second and related flow rates|cusecs]] of water for the arid rain shadow regions of present-day [[Theni]], [[Dindigul District]], [[Madurai District]], [[Sivaganga District]] and [[Ramanathapuram]] districts of [[Tamil Nadu]], then under British rule as part of Madras Province (Sandes, 1935). The Periyar project, as it was then known, was widely considered well into the 20th century as "one of the most extraordinary feats of engineering ever performed by man". A large amount of manual labour was involved and worker mortality from [[malaria]] was high. It was claimed that had it not been for "the medicinal effects of the native spirit called [[arrack]], the dam might never have been finished". Disease killed 483 people during the construction of this dam and were buried on-site in a cemetery just north of the dam. In 2012, it was announced that a memorial dedicated to dam engineer [[John Pennycuick (British engineer)|Pennycuick]] would be erected at the dam site.{{cite news|title=Jayalalithaa announces memorial for engineer who built Mullaperiyar dam|url=http://www.ndtv.com/article/tamil-nadu/jayalalithaa-announces-memorial-for-engineer-who-built-mullaperiyar-dam-164781?pfrom=home-india|access-date=9 January 2012|newspaper=[[NDTV]]|date=8 January 2012|archive-date=9 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120109083020/http://www.ndtv.com/article/tamil-nadu/jayalalithaa-announces-memorial-for-engineer-who-built-mullaperiyar-dam-164781?pfrom=home-india|url-status=live}} ==Protected area== The [[Periyar National Park]] in [[Thekkady]], a [[protected areas of Kerala|Protected area of Kerala]], is located around the dam's reservoir, the {{convert|26|km2|mi2|abbr=on}} Periyar lake. 62 different kinds of [[mammal]]s have been recorded in Periyar, including many threatened ones. Periyar is a highly protected [[Project Tiger|tiger reserve]] and hosts 35 [[Bengal tiger|tigers]] above two-years of age as of January 2017 in the reserve.{{cite news|title=35 tigers at Periyar Tiger Reserve: Survey|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/kochi/35-tigers-at-periyar-tiger-reserve-survey/articleshow/56362331.cms|website=Times of India|date=6 January 2017|access-date=16 January 2017|archive-date=8 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170108211030/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/kochi/35-tigers-at-periyar-tiger-reserve-survey/articleshow/56362331.cms|url-status=live}}{{cite web|title=Rare moments of Indian tiger family caught on camera trap|url=http://newsable.asianetnews.tv/south/tiger-census-periyar-tiger-reserve-35-tigers|website=Asianet Newsable|access-date=16 January 2017}} Declared an [[Project Elephant|elephant reserve]] on 2 April 2002,{{cite web |url=http://envfor.nic.in/pe/PE%20Note.pdf |title=Note on Project Elephant |year=2008 |work=Ministry of Environment & Forests, Government of India |access-date=9 January 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120312060920/http://envfor.nic.in/pe/PE%20Note.pdf |archive-date=12 March 2012}} the population of [[Indian elephant]]s in 2005 was estimated at 1100, however Periyar suffers greatly from poaching of elephant being the worst affected of South Indian sanctuaries.{{cite journal |last1=Ramakrishnan |first1=Uma |author2=Santosh, J. A. |author3=Ramakrishnan, Uma |author4=Sukumar, R. |date=25 January 1998 |title=The population and conservation status of Asian elephants in the Periyar Tiger Reserve, Southern India |journal=Current Science |volume=74 |issue=2 |pages=110–113 |url=http://eprints.iisc.ernet.in/1499/1/currsci.pdf |access-date=9 January 2012 |archive-date=17 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160117172804/http://eprints.iisc.ernet.in/1499/1/currsci.pdf |url-status=live }} Other mammals found here include [[gaur]], [[bison]], [[sambar deer|sambar]] (horse deer), [[barking deer]], [[mouse deer]], [[dhole]]s (Indian wild dogs), [[mongoose]], [[fox]]es and [[leopard]]s. Four species of primates are found at Periyar – the rare [[lion-tailed macaque]], the [[Nilgiri langur]], the common [[langur]], and the [[bonnet macaque]]. According to a report by the Kerala Forest Research Institute, the protected area surrounding the dam and reservoir is classified as a [[biodiversity hot spot]].{{cite web | url=http://www.kfri.org/main/library/publi/links/RR024.pdf | title=R1 | access-date=27 November 2011 }}{{Dead link|date=September 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ==Dam safety== After the 1979 [[Morvi dam failure|Morvi Dam failure]] which killed up to 15,000 people,{{cite book|author=World Bank. Environment Dept|title=Environmental assessment sourcebook|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QtSvTSHVxeQC&pg=PA86|access-date=10 January 2012|publisher=World Bank Publications |isbn=978-0-8213-1845-4 |page=86|year=1991}} safety concerns of the aging Mullaperiyar dam and alleged leaks and cracks in the structure were raised by the Kerala Government.{{Citation | title = Two states and a dam | url = http://business-standard.com/india/news/two-statesa-dam/457826/ | year = 2011 | journal = Business Standard | access-date = 9 December 2011 | last1 = Standard | archive-date = 12 March 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120312223717/http://www.business-standard.com/india/news/two-statesa-dam/457826/ | url-status = live }} A study conducted by The Centre for Earth Science Studies (CESS), [[Thiruvananthapuram]], had reported that the structure would not withstand an earthquake above magnitude 6 on the [[Richter scale]]. The dam was also inspected by the chairman, [[Central Water Commission]] (CWC). On the orders of the CWC, the Tamil Nadu government lowered the storage level from 152 feet to 142.2 feet then to 136 feet, conducted safety repairs and strengthened the dam. Strengthening measures adopted by Tamil Nadu PWD from 1979 with the recommendation of Central Water Commission (CWC) include grouting of the old dam with concrete, guniting the upstream face of dam, cable anchoring of the dam's structure with the foundation throughout its length, RCC(Reinforced Concrete Construction) capping on top of the dam at height above 145 feet, building 10 meter RCC concrete backing structure with 10 feet foundation up to height of 145 feet in downstream face of dam and binding the RCC structure using shear keys and concrete grouting with the old structure and the foundation along the downstream face of dam, building additional drainage galleries in order to measure seepage and additional sluice gates for water evacuation.{{Cite news |date=2012-01-02 |title=The case for a new Mullaperiyar dam |url=https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/op-ed/the-case-for-a-new-mullaperiyar-dam/article2769504.ece |access-date=2024-08-07 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}{{Cite web |date=2014-05-11 |title=Exclusive: Mullaperiyar dam was strengthened thrice and it's stronger than a new dam, says Justice K.T. Thomas |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/south/story/mullaperiyar-dam-k-t-thomas-exclusive-interview-with-india-today-192443-2014-05-11 |access-date=2024-08-07 |website=India Today |language=en}} During a 2011 scanning of the Mullaperiyar dam using a [[remotely operated vehicle]] by the Central Soil and Materials Research Station on directions from the Empowered Committee of the Supreme Court, the Kerala Government observer opined that "mistakes in the strengthening works carried out by Tamil Nadu" in 1979 damaged the masonry of the dam.{{Citation | title = 'Serious damage' to masonry of Mullaperiyar dam detected | url = http://www.thehindu.com/news/states/kerala/article2694645.ece | author = Mathew, Roy | journal = The Hindu | pages = 2011 | access-date = 9 December 2011 | date = 7 December 2011 | archive-date = 7 January 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120107205741/http://www.thehindu.com/news/states/kerala/article2694645.ece | url-status = live }} Current safety concerns relate to several issues. Since the dam was constructed using stone rubble masonry with lime mortar grouting following prevailing 19th-century construction techniques that have now become archaic, seepage and leaks from the dam have caused concern.{{Cite web |url=http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-kerala/article2648866.ece?textsize=large&test=1 |title=The Hindu, 22 November 2011, 'Tamilnadu seepage data wrong: says Mullaperiyar cell chairman' |website=[[The Hindu]] |access-date=30 November 2011 |archive-date=2 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131202230127/http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-kerala/article2648866.ece?textsize=large&test=1 |url-status=live }}{{Cite web |url=http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-kerala/article2697091.ece |title="Serious damage to masonry of dam detected", the Hindu, 7 Dec 2011 |website=[[The Hindu]] |access-date=8 December 2011 |archive-date=8 January 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120108042313/http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-kerala/article2697091.ece |url-status=live }} Moreover, the dam is situated in a seismically active zone.{{Cite web |url=http://geofizika-journal.gfz.hr/Vol_09/Singh.pdf |title=Singh, H.N., Raghavan, V., & Raju, G.K. These could be reservoir-induced seismicity, requiring further studies according to experts.{{Cite news |url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/states/kerala/article2647342.ece |title="Call for studies on reservoir-induced seismicity in Idukki", the Hindu, 21 November 2011 |newspaper=The Hindu |date=21 November 2011 |access-date=2 December 2011 |archive-date=22 November 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111122161738/http://www.thehindu.com/news/states/kerala/article2647342.ece |url-status=live }} A 2009 report by IIT Roorkee stated that the dam "was likely to face damage if an earthquake of the magnitude of 6.5 on the Richter scale struck its vicinity when the water level is at 136 feet".{{Citation | title = IIT, Roorkee report on Mullaperiyar says dam not safe | url = https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/thiruvananthapuram/IIT-Roorkee-report-on-Mullaperiyar-says-dam-not-safe-/articleshow/5172935.cms | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110811042201/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2009-10-28/thiruvananthapuram/28065845_1_new-dam-dam-issue-mullaperiyar-reservoir | url-status = live | archive-date = 11 August 2011 | access-date = 9 December 2011 | journal = [[The Times of India]] | date=28 October 2009}} ==Justice A.S. Anand Committee (Empowered Committee)== On 18 February 2010, the Supreme Court decided to constitute a five-member empowered committee consisting three judges and two technical experts to inspect and study all the issues of Mullaperiyar Dam and seek a report from it within six months.{{cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/article108195.ece|title=Supreme Court constitutes empowered committee to go into Mullaperiyar issues|last=Venkatesan|first=J.|date=17 February 2010|work=The Hindu|location=Chennai, India|access-date=26 June 2013|archive-date=18 March 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130318025243/http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/article108195.ece|url-status=live}} The Bench in its draft order said Tamil Nadu and Kerala would have the option to nominate a member each, who could be either a retired judge or a technical expert. The five-member committee will be headed by former Chief Justice of India [[Adarsh Sein Anand|A. S. Anand]] to go into all issues relating to the dam's safety and the storage level. The then late Tamil Nadu Chief Minister [[M. Karunanidhi]] said that immediately after the Supreme Court announced its decision to set up a committee, he had written to Congress president asking the centre to mediate between Kerala and Tamil Nadu on Mullaperiyar issue.{{cite news|url=http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2010-02-21/india/28133026_1_mullaperiyar-dam-inter-state-river-water-disputes-cauvery-issue|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105155218/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2010-02-21/india/28133026_1_mullaperiyar-dam-inter-state-river-water-disputes-cauvery-issue|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 November 2013|work=[[The Times of India]]|title=DMK against SC panel on dam|date=21 February 2010}} However, the then Leader of Opposition i.e., the late Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu [[J. Jayalalithaa]] objected to the TN Government move. She said that this would give advantage to Kerala in the issue.{{cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/article111203.ece|title=Jayalalithaa criticises Karunanidhi over Mullaperiyar issue|date=22 February 2010|work=The Hindu|location=Chennai, India|access-date=26 June 2013|archive-date=3 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203153633/http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/article111203.ece|url-status=live}} Meanwhile, Kerala Water Resources Minister [[N. K. Thomas to be on Mullaperiyar panel|date=4 March 2010|work=[[The Hindu]]|location=Chennai, India}} On 8 March 2010, Tamil Nadu told the Supreme Court that it was not interested in adjudicating the dispute with Kerala before the special "empowered" committee appointed by the apex court for settling the inter-State issue.{{cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/article221094.ece|title=Tamil Nadu not interested in adjudicating Mullaperiyar before panel|date=8 March 2010|work=The Hindu|location=Chennai, India|access-date=26 June 2013|archive-date=3 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203153641/http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/article221094.ece|url-status=live}} However, Supreme Court refused to accept Tamil Nadu's request to scrap the decision to form the empowered committee. The Supreme Court also criticized the Union Government on its reluctance in funding the empowered committee.{{cite news|url=http://www.hindu.com/2010/03/30/stories/2010033055571300.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100403033545/http://www.hindu.com/2010/03/30/stories/2010033055571300.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 April 2010|title=Tamil Nadu plea dismissed, empowered panel on Mullaperiyar will stay|date=30 March 2010|work=[[The Hindu]]|location=Chennai, India}} The Empowered Committee headed by the former Chief Justice of India A.S. Anand, in its findings concluded that the dam is "structurally, hydrologically safe, and Tamil Nadu can raise the water level from 136 to 142 feet after carrying out repairs."{{Cite news|url = https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/mullaperiyar-dam-structurally-hydrologically-safe-panel/article3353151.ece|title = Mullaperiyar dam structurally & hydrologically safe: Panel|newspaper = The Hindu|date = 25 April 2012|last1 = Venkatesan|first1 = J.|access-date = 18 September 2023|archive-date = 6 June 2023|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20230606162606/https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/mullaperiyar-dam-structurally-hydrologically-safe-panel/article3353151.ece|url-status = live}} ==Interstate dispute== {{Further|Tamil Nadu-Kerala dam row}} [[File:Padhathi pradesham.JPG|thumb|right|278x278px|Mullaperiyar reservoir]] The control and safety of the dam and the validity and fairness of the lease agreement have been points of [[Tamil Nadu-Kerala dam row|dispute between Kerala and Tamil Nadu states]].{{cite news |author=Roy Mathew |title=State is unprepared for disasters |url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/states/kerala/article2674541.ece |newspaper=the Hindu |publisher=Kasturi & Sons Ltd |access-date=6 December 2011 |date=30 November 2011 |location=Thiruvananthapuram, Chennai, India |archive-date=2 December 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111202232155/http://www.thehindu.com/news/states/kerala/article2674541.ece |url-status=live }} Supreme court judgment came on 27 February 2006, allowing [[Tamil Nadu]] to raise the level of the dam to {{Convert|152|ft|m|0|abbr=on}} after strengthening it. Responding to it, Mullaperiyar dam was declared an 'endangered' scheduled dam by the Kerala Government under the disputed Kerala Irrigation and Water Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2006.[http://www.kerenvis.nic.in/legislation/Microsoft%20Word%20-%20Act%202006.pdf The Kerala Irrigation And Water Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2006] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111216093842/http://www.kerenvis.nic.in/legislation/Microsoft%20Word%20-%20Act%202006.pdf |date=16 December 2011 }}. Tamil Nadu has insisted on raising the water level in the dam to 142 feet, pointing out crop failures. However, the court has clarified Tamil Nadu is not a riparian state. "In the process the farmers of the erstwhile rain shadow areas in Tamil Nadu who had started a thrice yearly cropping pattern had to go back to the bi-annual cropping."{{cite news |url=http://www.hardnewsmedia.com/portal/2006/03/413 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070113213632/http://www.hardnewsmedia.com/portal/2006/03/413 | archive-date=13 January 2007 | title=The Mullaperiyaru imbroglio | work=Hard News | first=ER | last=Gopinath | date=April 2006 | access-date=21 June 2021 }} The Kerala Government maintains that this is not true. During the year 1979–80 the gross area cultivated in Periyar command area was {{convert|171307|acre|km2}}. After the lowering of the level to {{convert|136|ft|m|abbr=on}}, the gross irrigated area increased and in 1994–95 it reached {{convert|229718|acre|km2}}.[http://expert-eyes.org/mullaperiyar.html Kerala Government's arguments] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070717010912/http://www.expert-eyes.org/mullaperiyar.html |date=17 July 2007 }}. In 2006, the [[Supreme Court of India]] by its decision by a three-member division bench, allowed for the storage level to be raised to {{convert|142|ft|m}} pending completion of the proposed strengthening measures, provision of other additional vents and implementation of other suggestions. However, the [[Government of Kerala|Kerala Government]] promulgated a new "Dam Safety Act" against increasing the storage level of the dam, which has been challenged by Tamil Nadu on various grounds. The Supreme Court issued notice to Kerala to respond, however did not stay the operation of the Act even as an interim measure. The Court then advised the States to settle the matter amicably, and adjourned hearing in order to enable them to do so. The Supreme Court of India termed the act as not unconstitutional.[https://web.archive.org/web/20070313155619/http://www.hindu.com/2006/09/09/stories/2006090911840400.htm Mullaperiyar: apex court issues notice to Government ]. The Hindu. 9 September 2006. Retrieved 25 November 2011. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court constituted a Constitution bench to hear the case considering its wide ramifications. Mullaperiyar Dam (IPA: [mulːɐpːeɾijɐːr]) is a masonry gravity dam on the Periyar River of Idukki district of Indian state of Kerala. It is situated 150 km south east of Kochi and 200 km north east of state capital city of Trivandrum. It is located 881 m (2,890 ft) above the sea level, on the Cardamom Hills of the Western Ghats in Thekkady, Idukki District of Kerala, India. 
It was constructed between 1887 and 1895 by workers under the command of Colonel John Pennycuick, and also reached in an agreement to divert water eastwards to the Madras Presidency area (present-day Tamil Nadu). It has a height of 53.6 m (176 ft) from the foundation, and a length of 365.7 m (1,200 ft). The Periyar National Park in Thekkady is located around the dam's reservoir. The dam is built at the confluence of Mullayar and Periyar rivers. The dam is located in Kerala on the river Periyar, but is operated and maintained by the neighbouring state of Tamil Nadu. Although the Periyar River has a total catchment area of 5398 km2 with 114 km2 downstream from the dam in Tamil Nadu, the catchment area of the Mullaperiyar Dam itself lies entirely in Kerala and thus the Periyar is not an inter-State river. On 21 November 2014, the water level hit 142 feet for the first time in 35 years. The reservoir again hit the maximum limit of 142 feet on 15 August 2018, following incessant rains in the state of Kerala. In a 2021 UNU-INWEH report about ageing large dams around the world, Mullaperiyar dam was said to be "situated in a seismically active area with significant structural flaws and poses risk to 5-10 million people if the 130+ years old dam were to fail".
